answers.answer: The table counts the splitter's own output. How many chunks a document produces is arithmetic over the document and the parameters, and it says nothing about whether anything was retrieved better. A measurement would name a corpus and a set of queries, name a retrieval metric such as nDCG or recall at k, and compare at least two configurations against each other with numbers and a direction.
accept: identifies chunk count as an output of the splitter rather than a retrieval outcome
says a real measurement names a retrieval metric such as nDCG or recall at k
says a real measurement compares two or more configurations on a stated corpus

answers.answer: They entitle you to say that this is what the LangChain tutorial ships as its starting configuration, which is a fine way to get a first pipeline running. They do not entitle you to say that 1000 and 200 perform well or beat any alternative, because the tutorial supplies no justification for either number anywhere in its text. A default carries only the evidence its source shipped with it.
accept: says the numbers are a published starting default, usable to get a pipeline running
says they carry no evidence, because the tutorial justifies neither number
says copying them is not a claim that 1000 or 200 beat any alternative

answers.answer: A page whose overlap figure came out of a single comparison on a single corpus has one figure to report. Two unreconciled figures on the same page about the same technique show the width of the band the authors accept rather than a measured value. Do not average the two, and do not treat either as a typo for the other; copying either one commits you to nothing the page has established.
accept: says the disagreement indicates the figures did not come from one measurement, or shows the range the authors accept
says not to average the two figures
says not to treat the difference as a typo or otherwise resolve it

answers.answer: It goes lower because of the token counts of that particular sample document, and it names a mechanical consequence of ignoring this: an overlap set too large can end up producing no overlap at all. The parameters did not change meaning; the document changed, and the same settings behaved differently on it. The right chunking parameters are a property of the pairing between the splitter and the documents, which is why the page also says the optimal choice depends on how the chunks are used.
accept: names the sample document's token counts as the reason for going below the recommendation
mentions that too large an overlap can result in no overlap appearing at all
concludes that the right parameters depend on the documents rather than on the splitter alone

answers.answer: The tutorial splits because its loaded documentation runs past 100,000 tokens, which does not fit the context window of many models, because models struggle to find information in very long inputs, and because spending the window on bulk content is not token efficient. That argues for splitting at all. It says nothing about where the boundary between 800 and 1200 should fall, and the tutorial offers no justification for the two values it then uses.
accept: gives the tutorial's reason: the corpus is too long for many context windows, models struggle to find information in very long inputs, or filling the window is not token efficient
says the reason supports splitting in general rather than any particular size or overlap
notes that the tutorial supplies no justification for 1000 or 200
